prompt:
I've received the comprehensive audit report from my coding agent. It includes:

- 36 Playwright screenshots (9 pages × desktop/mobile × viewport/full-page)
- Console error from the homepage: `<circle> attribute cx: Expected length, "undefined"`
- Complete codebase context (all components, CSS, project data, layout)
- The full audit findings organized by priority (P0-P2)

The audit's top recommendations are:
1. Fix mobile Engineering Network overlapping nodes
2. Fix mobile architecture text clipping in all 5 case studies
3. Add real contact info to the Contact page
4. Fix Home Security mobile connector bars
5. Add authentic engineering evidence to case studies
6. Improve Projects index with visual previews
7. Add ARM project to the index
8. Fix metadata inconsistencies

I'm ready to start implementing. What would you like me to tackle first — the P0 fixes, or do you have a different priority in mind?
response:
Start with the P0 fixes. Do not begin adding project previews, new case studies, or visual effects while confirmed rendering defects remain.

The first milestone should address the Engineering Network, mobile architecture clipping, and Home Security connectors. Include the homepage console error because it may indicate a broken SVG calculation.

Contact information is important, but do not invent an email address or resume URL. You can address that separately once the actual contact details are available.

The following instructions are for the coding agent.

MILESTONE 4 — CRITICAL RESPONSIVE AND SVG REPAIRS
Objective

Resolve the confirmed mobile rendering defects and investigate the homepage SVG console error without redesigning the website or disturbing previously verified desktop functionality.

Use the existing Next.js, React, Framer Motion, CSS, and Playwright setup. Do not install additional frameworks or introduce unnecessary abstractions.

Do not use subagents. Perform all work directly.

Completion checklist
1. Inspect the existing implementation
Inspect the current Git status, relevant components, CSS, and existing Playwright tests.
Review the latest audit screenshots and identify the exact components responsible for the reported defects.
Confirm the problems still exist in the current implementation before modifying code.
Preserve unrelated changes and all known-good desktop functionality.

Do not repeat investigations that have already established a confirmed root cause.

2. Fix the mobile Engineering Network

The audit found overlapping domain nodes in the mobile Engineering Network.

Inspect the current mobile network layout and its responsive CSS.
Identify the positioning or sizing rules responsible for overlapping nodes.
Fix the mobile layout so all eight domains have sufficient space and remain readable.
Ensure the connections remain aligned with their intended nodes.
Preserve desktop node positions, selection behavior, connection highlighting, and detail-panel functionality.
Test the mobile layout at 375px and 390px viewport widths.

Use the existing mobile layout wherever possible. Do not rebuild the desktop network or introduce a new visualization system.

3. Fix mobile architecture clipping across the five case studies

The audit identified architecture text extending beyond its container on mobile project pages.

Identify the shared component or CSS responsible for rendering project architecture sequences.
Fix the underlying responsive layout instead of applying separate patches to every project page.
Allow architecture steps to wrap or form a vertical sequence on narrow screens.
Ensure every component name and connection remains visible.
Verify the fix on Home Security, Ultrasonic, Joystick, FPGA, and Power Engineering case studies.
Preserve the existing desktop architecture presentation.

Do not reduce the font size until the text fits. The architecture must remain readable.

4. Fix the Home Security mobile connectors

The audit identified full-width horizontal connector bars appearing between vertically stacked subsystems.

Inspect the responsive connector styles and the current architecture DOM structure.
Determine why desktop-oriented connectors remain horizontal on mobile.
Replace those mobile connector presentations with correctly aligned vertical connections.
Preserve the actual sequential data flow and directional indicators.
Verify the Raspberry Pi services branch and Mobile App endpoint.
Confirm the desktop architecture remains unchanged and functional.

Do not redesign the five-row desktop architecture.

5. Investigate and fix the homepage SVG console error

The audit recorded:

<circle> attribute cx: Expected length, "undefined"

A circle is receiving an undefined value for its horizontal position.

Reproduce the error in the current browser session.
Identify the exact SVG circle and React component responsible.
Trace the coordinate value to its source.
Determine why the value becomes undefined.
Correct the underlying calculation, initialization, or data mapping.
Verify that the circle receives a valid coordinate in every supported state.
Check that the correction preserves the intended animation and SVG positioning.
Confirm the console error no longer occurs after refresh, scrolling, resizing, and interaction.

Do not simply suppress the console error or hide the circle.

If the error cannot be reproduced, document the attempted reproduction and evidence rather than modifying unrelated SVG code.

6. Browser verification and regression testing

Use the existing Playwright setup.

Verify the homepage at 375px, 390px, 768px, and 1280px viewport widths.
Verify all five case-study architecture sections on desktop and mobile.
Confirm no unintended horizontal overflow, text clipping, or node overlap.
Test Engineering Network node selection, connection highlighting, and detail-panel updates.
Verify the Home Security architecture and its scroll-driven activation.
Check that the Mobile App endpoint becomes visible.
Verify keyboard navigation and reduced-motion behavior for affected components.
Check the browser console for new errors.
Run the existing lint and production build checks.

Capture focused before-and-after screenshots of the affected sections.

If previously working functionality breaks, stop forward progress and identify the most recent relevant change. Fix or revert that regression before continuing.

Do not continue adding unrelated corrections while a regression remains unresolved.

7. Create the detailed milestone handoff

Create:

docs/handoffs/15d-critical-responsive-svg-repairs.md

The handoff must include the milestone objective, starting state, confirmed root causes, exact changes performed, reasons for those changes, relevant files, browser observations, before-and-after screenshots, verification results, regression checks, errors, deviations, and remaining work.

Record any unresolved or unverified issue explicitly.

Preserve the final screenshots somewhere persistent within the project rather than relying exclusively on temporary files.

8. Commit the verified milestone
Inspect Git status and preserve unrelated changes.
Stage only the intended source changes, tests, and handoff.
Inspect the staged diff.
Commit the completed and verified milestone.
Verify the commit hash and message.
Verify the final repository state.

Do not create separate commits for every small CSS adjustment.

9. Send the complete report through ask_chatgpt

After completing the milestone, send a full report containing:

MILESTONE: Critical responsive and SVG repairs.

OBJECTIVE: What was intended.

STARTING STATE: Confirmed defects.

ACTIONS: Exact changes performed and why.

ROOT CAUSES: Evidence supporting the identified causes.

BROWSER EVIDENCE: Before-and-after screenshots, computed dimensions, SVG coordinates, and actual visual observations.

VERIFICATION: Desktop, mobile, keyboard, reduced-motion, console, lint, and build results.

REGRESSION CHECKS: Previously working functionality retested and its actual results.

OUTCOME: PASS, FAIL, PARTIAL, or BLOCKED.

GIT: Commit hash, commit message, handoff path, and final repository state.

DEVIATIONS: Anything that differed from these instructions.

REMAINING WORK: Outstanding problems and the recommended next action.

COMPLETED CHECKLIST: Report PASS, FAIL, PARTIAL, or BLOCKED for every checklist item above. Do not mark an item complete unless it was actually verified.

STOP after sending the report through ask_chatgpt. Do not begin the next milestone until I review the results.

Once this milestone is verified, the next priority will be completing contact and resume access, followed by strengthening the engineering evidence and presentation of the five case studies.
